prompt: My canvas bag is (small) than that suitcase, so it fits under the seat.
explanation_ru: Односложное прилагательное «small» образует сравнительную степень с помощью суффикса -er: smaller.

prompt: Could you pass the grey towel? It looks (dry) than the striped one.
explanation_ru: У односложного прилагательного «dry» конечная «y» после согласной меняется на «i» перед суффиксом -er: drier.

prompt: Our attic bedroom doesn't get (hot) than the kitchen, even in July.
explanation_ru: В коротком прилагательном «hot» (согласная + краткая гласная + согласная) последняя согласная удваивается перед -er: hotter.

prompt: Does the glass lift move (slowly) than the old one near reception?
explanation_ru: Наречия на -ly образуют сравнительную степень с помощью «more»: more slowly.

prompt: We chose the soft armchair because it is ___ than the wooden bench.
explanation_ru: Длинное прилагательное «comfortable» образует сравнительную степень с «more» (more comfortable); форма «comfortabler» неверна, а «most» используется для превосходной степени.

prompt: That corner shop isn't more cheap than the big supermarket near the station.
answer: That corner shop isn't cheaper than the big supermarket near the station.
accepted_answers: That corner shop isn't cheaper than the big supermarket near the station.
That corner shop is not cheaper than the big supermarket near the station.
explanation_ru: Типичная ошибка — «more cheap»: односложное прилагательное «cheap» образует сравнительную степень через суффикс -er (cheaper).

prompt: Our sofa wouldn't fit through the front entrance, which is (narrow) than the garden gate, so moving took (long).
explanation_ru: Двусложное прилагательное «narrow» на -ow обычно принимает -er (narrower, допустимо и more narrow), а краткое наречие «long» всегда образует форму longer.

prompt: Once our technician cleaned the rollers, the office scanner worked (reliably) than before and broke down (little) often.
explanation_ru: Наречие на -ly «reliably» требует «more» (more reliably), а у «little» неправильная сравнительная степень — less.

prompt: Although Tariq's second delivery plan was (clever) than our original timetable, the vans still reached the warehouse (late) than before.
explanation_ru: Двусложное «clever» допускает обе формы — cleverer и more clever; у наречия «late» сравнительная степень образуется добавлением -r: later.

prompt: Honestly, I didn't laugh because the second comedy sketch was ___ than the opening one.
explanation_ru: В прилагательном «silly» конечная «y» меняется на «i» перед -er (sillier); частые ошибки — сохранить «y» (sillyer) или добавить лишнее «more».

prompt: Everyone assumes Priya runs the family bakery, although her brother is three years ___ than her.
explanation_ru: Перед союзом «than» всегда используется «older»; форма «elder» ставится только перед существительным-родственником и с «than» не употребляется.

prompt: Isn't this community hall biger than the library room we booked for our autumn quiz?
answer: Isn't this community hall bigger than the library room we booked for our autumn quiz?
accepted_answers: Isn't this community hall bigger than the library room we booked for our autumn quiz?
explanation_ru: Типичная орфографическая ошибка — «biger»: в коротком прилагательном «big» конечная согласная «g» удваивается перед -er (bigger).

prompt: We packed our cameras in a metal box for the coach trip. Two people had to lift it, yet none of the lenses cracked unlike in the soft bag.
options: The metal box was lighter than the soft bag, so the cameras travelled more safely.
The metal box was heavyer than the soft bag, so the cameras travelled safelyer.
The metal box was heavier than the soft bag, yet the cameras travelled more safely inside it.
The metal box was the heaviest of all bags, yet the cameras broke more easily inside it.
explanation_ru: Подходит только третий вариант: у «heavy» буква «y» меняется на «i» (heavier), а наречие «safely» образует сравнительную степень с «more» (more safely), что точно отражает ситуацию.

prompt: No room in the town library feels as cosy as the small corner study. → The small corner study is …
answer: The small corner study is the cosiest room in the town library.
accepted_answers: The small corner study is the cosiest room in the town library.
The small corner study is the most cosy room in the town library.
explanation_ru: Для превосходной степени прилагательного «cosy» конечная «y» меняется на «i» перед -est: the cosiest.

prompt: "Did Samira check the new building rules before the meeting?" "Yes, she prepared (carefully) than anyone else on our team. Her plan wasn't cheap, though it saved (much) money than Pavel's idea. In fact, it turned out to be (good) proposal we received all month."
explanation_ru: Наречие на -ly образует форму с «more» (more carefully), а у «much» и «good» неправильные степени сравнения: more и the best.

prompt: Switching to the updated workshop fan solved two headaches at once. Because the new display is (simple) to read than the old one, even a trainee can operate it without asking for help. On top of that, the redesigned motor runs (quietly) than the previous model while using (little) power during long shifts. Nobody in the workshop misses the loud rattle we endured before.
explanation_ru: Двусложное «simple» принимает -er (simpler, возможно и more simple), наречие «quietly» требует «more», а неисчисляемое «little» имеет неправильную форму less.

prompt: Dear Mateo, I viewed several new flats near the river before lunch. The ground-floor one is (affordable) on my shortlist, although it sits (far) from the station than the advert claimed. Sadly, there are (few) evening buses there than on my current street, so commuting wouldn't be easy. Let me know which one you prefer.
explanation_ru: Длинное прилагательное «affordable» образует превосходную степень с «the most», у «far» для расстояния подходят further и farther, а с исчисляемым «buses» ставится fewer.

prompt: Local residents discussed four ideas for updating the market square. The council's latest design is (ambitious) of all, yet its budget summary looks (confusing) than the draft from spring. Several key figures are missing, so the team presented the costs (badly) than we expected. Without real numbers, nobody will support the plan.
explanation_ru: Многосложные «ambitious» и «confusing» образуют степени сравнения с «the most» и «more», а у наречия «badly» неправильная сравнительная степень — worse.
